The loop structure: for each gate → skip disabled/skippable → while(true) attempts++ → run → on error: if attempts>max || noRetry → non-blocking? record : return failure; else resume → if !resume.atempted → non-blocking? record : return failure; if returnAfterResume → return failure+resumeAttempted; else loop again.

A clean decomposition:

```js
function failureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   return { success: false, failedGate: name, error: errorText, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}

function recordNonBlockingFailure(name, attempts, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   console.warn(...);
   results.push({ name: name, success: false, attempts: attempts, error: errorText, blocking: false });
   nonBlockingFailures.push({ name: name, error: errorText });
}
``

`runGateAttempt(gate, name, command, workingDir, gateType)` → try runCommand, log; return {ok:true, output} or {ok:false, errorText}.

Then runConfiguredGates:

```js
function runConfiguredGates(options, section, stagePrefix) {
   options = options || {};
   section = section || 'qualityGates';
   stagePrefix = stagePrefix || 'quality_gate';
   var gateType = section === 'policyGates' ? 'policy gate' : 'quality gate';
   var customParams = options.customParams || {};
   var config = normalizeConfig(customParams, options.section || section);
   var gates = getConfiguredGates(customParams, options.section || section, section);
   var results = [];
   var nonBlockingFailures = [];
   for (var i = 0; i < gates.length; i++) {
       var outcome = runGate(gates[i], i, { options, section, stagePrefix, gateType, config, customParams, results, nonBlockingFailures });
       if (outcome) return outcome; // a failure result to bubble
   }
   return { success: true, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}
``

1. **no-args defaults**: `runConfiguredGates()` → success true, empty results. Also pins section default 'qualityGates' and stagePrefix 'quality_gate' (implicitly through gate runs? A no-arg call with gates can't be configured — customParams absent → no gates. So just empty success.)

If scoped section has `gates`, config.gates = scoped gates. If root has `gates` (i.e. `feedbackLoop.gates`), merged.gates too. `config[section]` — scoped section object itself? normalizeConfig: merged gets root scalar/array keys; then scoped keys override. `config.qualityGates` would only exist if root.qualityGates is an array (copied as-is since Array → treated as scalar!) — e.g. `feedbackLoop: { qualityGates: [gate,...] }` → normalizeConfig copies root.qualityGates (array → typeof 'object' BUT Array.isArray → skipped!). # Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository …

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true

Plan for `runConfiguredGates` (comp 37): extract pure helpers:
- `resolveGateCommand(gate, ticketKey)` → command string or null
- `resolveGateWorkingDir(gate, options, config)` 
- `gateMaxAttempts(gate)` 
- `buildGateFeedbackConfig(section, gate, maxAttempts)` → feedbackLoopConfig object
- `buildGateResumeOptions(options, section, stagePrefix, name, gate, maxAttempts, command, workingDir, errorText)` → resumeAgent options... 
- `gateFailureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures)` → the blocking failure return object
- `nonBlockingFailure(gateType, name, attempts, errorText)` handling — pushes to results/nonBlockingFailures (impure-ish but fine as helper taking arrays)
- The per-gate run loop → maybe extract `runSingleGate(gate, ctx)` returning either {done:true,...} or continuation info.

The loop structure: for each gate → skip disabled/skippable → while(true) attempts++ → run → on error: if attempts>max || noRetry → non-blocking? record : return failure; else resume → if !resume.atempted → non-blocking? record : return failure; if returnAfterResume → return failure+resumeAttempted; else loop again.

A clean decomposition:

```js
function failureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   return { success: false, failedGate: name, error: errorText, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}

function recordNonBlockingFailure(name, attempts, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   console.warn(...);
   results.push({ name: name, success: false, attempts: attempts, error: errorText, blocking: false });
   nonBlockingFailures.push({ name: name, error: errorText });
}
``

`runGateAttempt(gate, name, command, workingDir, gateType)` → try runCommand, log; return {ok:true, output} or {ok:false, errorText}.

`shouldRetryGate(gate, attempts, maxAttempts)` → attempts <= max && gate.retryWithAgent !== false.

`gateResumeCustomParams(section, gate, maxAttempts)`.

Then runConfiguredGates:

```js
function runConfiguredGates(options, section, stagePrefix) {
   options = options || {};
   section = section || 'qualityGates';
   stagePrefix = stagePrefix || 'quality_gate';
   var gateType = section === 'policyGates' ? 'policy gate' : 'quality gate';
   var customParams = options.customParams || {};
   var config = normalizeConfig(customParams, options.section || section);
   var gates = getConfiguredGates(customParams, options.section || section, section);
   var results = [];
   var nonBlockingFailures = [];
   for (var i = 0; i < gates.length; i++) {
       var outcome = runGate(gates[i], i, { options, section, stagePrefix, gateType, config, customParams, results, nonBlockingFailures });
       if (outcome) return outcome; // a failure result to bubble
   }
   return { success: true, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}
``

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          e…

2. Write characterization tests covering every branch.

CRAP <= 8 with complexity C and coverage cov: CRAP = C^2 * (1-cov)^3 + C. For C=4, fully covered: CRAP = 4. For C=2: 2. For C=3, cov=1: 3.

For a function with complexity ~9 fully covered → CRAP 9 > 8. Hmm, so I need either full coverage with complexity <= 8, or partial coverage. E.g., complexity 8 fully covered = 8. OK.

So each extracted helper needs complexity <= 8 with 100% coverage (hard but doable), or lower complexity.

Let me check: comp=7, CRAP 41.7 → 49*(1-cov)^3 + 7 = 41.7 → (1-cov)^3 = 34.7/49 = 0.708 → 1-cov = 0.891 → cov = 0.109. Hmm, that seems too low coverage. Maybe comp=9: 81*(1-cov)^3+9 = 41.7 → (1-cov)^3 = 0.404 → 1-cov=0.739 → cov=0.26.

Plan for `runConfiguredGates` (comp 37): extract pure helpers:
- `resolveGateCommand(gate, ticketKey)` → command string or null
- `resolveGateWorkingDir(gate, options, config)`

- `buildGateFeedbackConfig(section, gate, maxAttempts)` → feedbackLoopConfig object

- `gateFailureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures)` → the blocking failure return object
- `nonBlockingFailure(gateType, name, attempts, errorText)` handling — pushes to results/nonBlockingFailures (impure-ish but fine as helper taking arrays)
- The per-gate run loop → maybe extract `runSingleGate(gate, ctx)` returning either {done:true,...} or continuation info.

The loop structure: for each gate → skip disabled/skippable → while(true) attempts++ → run → on error: if attempts>max || noRetry → non-blocking? record : return failure; else resume → if !resume.atempted → non-blocking? record : return failure; if returnAfterResume → return failure+resumeAttempted; else loop again.

A clean decomposition:

```js
function failureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   return { success: false, failedGate: name, error: errorText, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}

function recordNonBlockingFailure(name, attempts, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   console.warn(...);
   results.push({ name: name, success: false, attempts: attempts, error: errorText, blocking: false });
   nonBlockingFailures.push({ name: name, error: errorText });
}
``

`runGateAttempt(gate, name, command, workingDir, gateType)` → try runCommand, log; return {ok:true, output} or {ok:false, errorText}.

`shouldRetryGate(gate, attempts, maxAttempts)` → attempts <= max && gate.retryWithAgent !== false.

Then runConfiguredGates:

```js
function runConfiguredGates(options, section, stagePrefix) {
   options = options || {};
   section = section || 'qualityGates';
   stagePrefix = stagePrefix || 'quality_gate';
   var gateType = section === 'policyGates' ? 'policy gate' : 'quality gate';
   var customParams = options.customParams || {};
   var config = normalizeConfig(customParams, options.section || section);
   var gates = getConfiguredGates(customParams, options.section || section, section);
   var results = [];
   var nonBlockingFailures = [];
   for (var i = 0; i < gates.length; i++) {
       var outcome = runGate(gates[i], i, { options, section, stagePrefix, gateType, config, customParams, results, nonBlockingFailures });
       if (outcome) return outcome; // a failure result to bubble
   }
   return { success: true, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}
``

And runGate contains the while loop; its complexity: conditions: gate && gate.enabled===false (2), command truthy, while loop, try/catch, attempts>max||retryWithAgent===false (2), !isBlocking, resume.atempted, returnAfterResume||...||... Behavior details to preserve:
1. console.log('Running ' + gateType + ' "' + name + '": ' + command) BEFORE each runCommand attempt (including retries).
2. On success: results.push({name, success:true, attempts, output: output || ''}). Note `runCommand(...) || ''` — output coerced to ''.
3. On throw: errorText = e && e.message ? e.message : String(e).

'\nWorking directory: ' + workingDir : '') + '\n' + errorText.

- gate B: no gate.workingDir → 'opt-dir'.

cli mock records full args. config.workingDir comes from normalizeConfig — scoped section object feedbackLoop: { qualityGates: { enabled: true, workingDir: 'cfg-dir', gates: [...] } → merged.workingDir = 'cfg-dir'. ✓

Test maxAttempts '3' string: fails twice, succeeds third → attempts 3, marker '2'.

Test retryWithAgent:false:
- blocking: gate throws once → return {success:false, failedGate, error}; commands length 1 (no mkdir, no run-agent).
- non-blocking: two gates [retry-no (blocking:false), next (ok)] → success true, nonBlockingFailures [name], next gate ran.

Test non-recoverable: gate fails with error text containing 'Bad credentials':
- blocking → {success:false, failedGate, error contains 'Bad credentials'}; commands: gate cmd + mkdir? wait — resumeAgent: isNonRecoverable checked BEFORE ensureFeedbackDir → no mkdir. So commands = [gate cmd].
- non-blocking → nonBlockingFailures entry; warn path '(no resume attempted)'.

Test attempts-exhausted: pre-set files['outputs/feedback/TS-xh_quality_gate_x.atempt'] = '2', maxAttempts 2 → gate throws → resume attempted=false (exhausted) → blocking failure; commands [gate cmd] only.

Test returnAfterResume (3 sources): each → {success:false, resumeAttempted:true, ...}; commands include mkdir + run-agent.sh; marker '1'.
- options: { returnAfterResume: true }
- gate: { returnAfterResume: true }
- config: feedbackLoop: { qualityGates: { returnAfterResume: true, ... }

Test non-Error throws: cli throws 'plain fail' → blocking failure error === 'plain fail'. Also throw object {custom:'x'} without message → String({custom:'x'}) === '[object Object]'.

Test output null → ': command returns null → results[0].output === ''. The default mock returns '' — || '' → ''. Use custom mock returning null.

Test results shape: [{name:'a', success:true, attempts:1, output:''}, ...]. And after non-blocking failure: {name:'spot', success:false, attempts:2, error:..., blocking:false} — attempts: gate maxAttempts 1 → fail(1) → resume → fail(2) → attempts>1 → non-blocking record with attempts 2.

Test legacy root-section array: customParams: { qualityGates: [{name:'legacy', command:'echo legacy'}] } via runQualityGates → ran. Hmm wait — getConfiguredGates(customParams, section='qualityGates', legacyKey='qualityGates'): config = normalizeConfig(customParams, 'qualityGates') — root keys copied: customParams.qualityGates is array → copied to merged.qualityGates; scoped = root.qualityGates (array, typeof object) → Object.keys of array → merged['0'], merged['1']... then gates = config.gates (undefined) || config['qualityGates'] (the array!) → ✓ runs.

Test section-named array: customParams: { feedbackLoop: { qualityGates: [{name:'sec', command:'echo sec'}] } → same path — also merged.qualityGates. Hmm — both tests hit the same `config[section]` branch. The `customParams[legacyKey]` distinct branch: gates must come from customParams[legacyKey] where legacyKey = section — when normalizeConfig does NOT produce config[section]... e.g. customParams: { qualityGates: [...] } DOES produce config[section] (root copy). To hit the third fallback: need config.gates and config[section] both falsy but customParams[section] truthy — impossible since normalizeConfig copies root arrays... UNLESS customParams[section] is a non-array non-null value like a STRING? normalizeConfig: `typeof root[key] !== 'object'` → string copied → config[section] = string → truthy → gates = string → not array → []. Hmm.

What about legacyKey different from section? getConfiguredGates(customParams, section, legacyKey) — called as (customParams, options.section || section, section) — legacyKey ALWAYS === section in runConfiguredGates. And runFeedbackLoop's other call? getConfiguredGates is only called from runConfiguredGates. So the third term fires only when config.gates and config[section] are both falsy while customParams[section] is truthy — given normalizeConfig copies arrays/scalars from root, config[section] truthy whenever customParams[section] truthy... EXCEPT when customParams[section] is null/undefined/false/'' (falsy) — then third term also falsy. So the third term is DEAD in practice — unreachable? Actually if customParams[legacyKey] is an ARRAY: config[section] = that array (truthy) → second term wins. If it's an object: normalizeConfig skips objects (typeof object && !array → not copied) → config[section] falsy; scoped = root[section] (object) → merged gets its keys (maybe gates!) → config.gates could win. If scoped object has no gates and root has no gates... then customParams[legacyKey] = object truthy → gates = the OBJECT → not array → []. Covers the third TERM being truthy but non-array → []. 

So to cover the third term of `||`: customParams: { qualityGates: { gates: undefined }... normalizeConfig({qualityGates: {...}}, 'qualityGates'): root keys — qualityGates is plain object → skipped; scoped = the object → keys copied (gates: undefined → merged.gates = undefined). gates = config.gates (undefined) || config['qualityGates'] (undefined) || customParams['qualityGates'] (the OBJECT — truthy) → object → not array → []. ✓ Covers third term. Test: gates object → success true, zero commands.

And Array.isArray false branch — covered by same test.

The loop structure: for each gate → skip disabled/skippable → while(true) attempts++ → run → on error: if attempts>max || noRetry → non-blocking? record : return failure; else resume → if !resume.atempted → non-blocking? record : return failure; if returnAfterResume → return failure+resumeAttempted; else loop again.

A clean decomposition:

```js
function failureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   return { success: false, failedGate: name, error: errorText, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}

function recordNonBlockingFailure(name, attempts, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   console.warn(...);
   results.push({ name: name, success: false, attempts: attempts, error: errorText, blocking: false });
   nonBlockingFailures.push({ name: name, error: errorText });
}
``

`runGateAttempt(gate, name, command, workingDir, gateType)` → try runCommand, log; return {ok:true, output} or {ok:false, errorText}.

function runConfiguredGates(options, section, stagePrefix) {
   options = options || {};

   stagePrefix = stagePrefix || 'quality_gate';
   var gateType = section === 'policyGates' ? 'policy gate' : 'quality gate';
   var customParams = options.customParams || {};
   var config = normalizeConfig(customParams, options.section || section);
   var gates = getConfiguredGates(customParams, options.section || section, section);
   var results = [];
   var nonBlockingFailures = [];
   for (var i = 0; i < gates.length; i++) {

       if (outcome) return outcome; // a failure result to bubble
   }

}
``

2. On success: results.push({name, success:true, attempts, output: output || ''}). Note `runCommand(...) || ''` — output coerced to ''.

- gate: { returnAfterResume: true }

Plan for `runConfiguredGates` (comp 37): extract pure helpers:
- `resolveGateCommand(gate, ticketKey)` → command string or null

The loop structure: for each gate → skip disabled/skippable → while(true) attempts++ → run → on error: if attempts>max || noRetry → non-blocking? record : return failure; else resume → if !resume.atempted → non-blocking? record : return failure; if returnAfterResume → return failure+resumeAttempted; else loop again.

function failureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {

}

function recordNonBlockingFailure(name, attempts, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {

function runConfiguredGates(options, section, stagePrefix) {
   options = options || {};
   section = section || 'qualityGates';
   stagePrefix = stagePrefix || 'quality_gate';
   var gateType = section === 'policyGates' ? 'policy gate' : 'quality gate';
   var customParams = options.customParams || {};
   var config = normalizeConfig(customParams, options.section || section);
   var gates = getConfiguredGates(customParams, options.section || section, section);
   var results = [];
   var nonBlockingFailures = [];
   for (var i = 0; i < gates.length; i++) {
       var outcome = runGate(gates[i], i, { options, section, stagePrefix, gateType, config, customParams, results, nonBlockingFailures });
       if (outcome) return outcome; // a failure result to bubble
   }
   return { success: true, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}
``

2. On success: results.push({name, success:true, attempts, output: output || ''}). Note `runCommand(...) || ''` — output coerced to ''.

'\nWorking directory: ' + workingDir : '') + '\n' + errorText.

Characterization tests for runConfiguredGates (current uncovered branches):

1. **no-args defaults**: `runConfiguredGates()` → success true, empty results. Also pins section default 'qualityGates' and stagePrefix 'quality_gate' (implicitly through gate runs? A no-arg call with gates can't be configured — customParams absent → no gates. So just empty success.)
2. **gate entry filtering**: null gate skipped; `{enabled:false}` skipped; gate without command skipped → zero commands.
3. **default gate name** `gate_1`/`gate_2` (index-based) — pin via result entry name and feedback prompt path.
4. **{ticketKey} substitution** in command.
5. **workingDir precedence**: gate.workingDir wins over options.workingDir; options.workingDir wins over config.workingDir; config.workingDir alone used.
6. **maxAttempts parsing**: null → 2 (default); string '3' → 3; garbage 'abc' → 0 → first failure fails immediately with NO resume (atempts=1 > 0) blocking.
7. **retryWithAgent:false**: blocking → immediate return failure, no mkdir feedback dir call (no resume); non-blocking → recorded as non-blocking failure, continue to next gate.
8. **no-resume path via non-recoverable error**: gate fails with 'Bad credentials' error text → resumeAgent returns non-recoverable → blocking gate → return failure with failedGate; non-blocking → 'no resume attempted' warn + record.
9. **no-resume via attempts-exhausted** (marker file pre-set at max) → same.
10. **returnAfterResume** via options.returnAfterResume=true → result has resumeAttempted:true; via gate.returnAfterResume=true; via config (feedbackLoop.<section>.returnAfterResume) → same.
11. **error object without message**: throwing a plain string → errorText = String(e).
12. **success output null → ''**: command returns undefined → result.output === ''.
13. **results accumulated across gates in order** (success + non-blocking failure).
14. **resume attempt counting within gate**: after one resume+retry success, result.atempts === 2 (covered by existing 'runs quality gate, resumes on first failure').

Also `getConfiguredGates` legacy keys:
15. gates via `feedbackLoop.qualityGates` scoped section (normalizeConfig merge) — covered partially by existing? Existing tests configure `feedbackLoop: { qualityGates: { enabled: true, gates: [...] }` → normalizeConfig picks scoped into merged; `config.gates` — scoped keys are flattened into merged config (merged[key] = scoped[key]) so config.gates works. The `customParams[legacyKey]` fallback (legacy: `customParams.qualityGates` array at root) is NOT covered. Test: `customParams: { qualityGates: [{name:'legacy', command:'echo legacy'}] }` with runQualityGates... wait but isFeedbackEnabled isn't checked in runConfiguredGates! Interesting — runConfiguredGates does NOT check isFeedbackEnabled. It just runs gates. So legacy array works regardless of enabled flag. Pin: legacy array runs.
16. non-array gates (`gates: {}`) → [] → success true.

Hmm wait — actually there's subtlety in getConfiguredGates with normalizeConfig: `normalizeConfig(customParams, section)` merges root scalars + scoped object. If scoped section has `gates`, config.gates = scoped gates. If root has `gates` (i.e. `feedbackLoop.gates`), merged.gates too. `config[section]` — scoped section object itself? normalizeConfig: merged gets root scalar/array keys; then scoped keys override. `config.qualityGates` would only exist if root.qualityGates is an array (copied as-is since Array → treated as scalar!) — e.g. `feedbackLoop: { qualityGates: [gate,...] }` → normalizeConfig copies root.qualityGates (array → typeof 'object' BUT Array.isArray → skipped!). Wait: `if (typeof root[key] !== 'object' || Array.isArray(root[key])) merged[key] = root[key];` — arrays ARE copied. So `merged.qualityGates = [gate]`. Then scoped = root[section] — for section='qualityGates', scoped = root.qualityGates which is an ARRAY — `typeof root[section] === 'object'` → true for array! `(section && root[section] && typeof root[section] === 'object')` → scoped = the array. Then `Object.keys(scoped).forEach(merged[key] = scoped[key])` — keys '0','1',... merged['0'] = gate. Weird but harmless-ish. Then getConfiguredGates: config.gates || config[section] (merged.qualityGates = the array!) → gates found. OK.

So test 16 variant: `customParams: { feedbackLoop: { qualityGates: [ {name:'x', command:'echo x'} ] }` — the array form at feedbackLoop.qualityGates → runs. That's the `config[section]` branch of getConfiguredGates.

17. Gates given as non-array (e.g. `gates: 'not-array'`) → [] — the Array.isArray false branch.

The parity harness uses `review_verdict_publish.js` (which requires `./review_verdict.js`) and only uses `unwrap` and `applyReviewVerdict` from it. The publish entry uses `DEFAULT_RUN_OUTPUT`, `unwrap`, `applyReviewVerdict`.

Now, TDD phase 1: write the characterization tests. Let me append them to both test files. I must use GralJS-compatible syntax (var, functions, no template literals, no arrow functions) since they run under dmtools too.

Let me write the feedbackLoop characterization tests first. I need to be careful with exact expected values:

Test: no-args → `runConfiguredGates()`:
- options = {} → customParams {} → normalizeConfig({}, 'qualityGates') → gates [] → success true, results [], nonBlockingFailures [].

Test: null/disabled/commandless gate entries: gates [null, {enabled:false, command:'echo a'}, {name:'no-cmd'}]:
- i=0: !gate → continue; i=1: enabled===false → continue; i=2: command null → continue.
- commands stays [] (cli mock not called). Result success true.

Test: unnamed gates indexed: gates [{command:'echo one'}, {command:'echo two'}]:
- names gate_1, gate_2. results[0].name === 'gate_1'. Marker path for a resume... simpler: both succeed → results names + order. Note: without `enabled` gates run even if feedbackLoop not "enabled" (runConfiguredGates doesn't check isFeedbackEnabled!) — correct: no enabled check in runConfiguredGates. ✓

Test: {ticketKey} substitution: gate command 'echo {ticketKey}', ticketKey 'TS-KY' → command executed 'echo TS-KY'.

Test: workingDir precedence — 3 gates:
- gate A: workingDir 'gate-dir', options.workingDir 'opt-dir', config workingDir 'cfg-dir' → ran with 'gate-dir'.
- gate B: no gate.workingDir → 'opt-dir'.
- gate C: no gate/options → 'cfg-dir'.
- gate D: none anywhere → null (undefined workingDirectory in args — runCommand only sets when workingDir truthy → args lacks workingDirectory).
cli mock records full args. config.workingDir comes from normalizeConfig — scoped section object feedbackLoop: { qualityGates: { enabled: true, workingDir: 'cfg-dir', gates: [...] } → merged.workingDir = 'cfg-dir'. ✓

Test maxAttempts null → default 2: gate maxAttempts null, fails once then succeeds → attempts 2; marker 'outputs/feedback/TS-def_quality_gate_mnull.atempt' === '1'. And resumeAgent's config maxAttempts=2.

Test maxAttempts '3' string: fails twice, succeeds third → attempts 3, marker '2'.

Test maxAttempts garbage 'abc' → 0 → no resume: command throws always → blocking failure, failedGate name, error message; commands contains NO 'mkdir -p outputs/feedback' (no ensureFeedbackDir — wait, ensureFeedbackDir is inside resumeAgent — not called → no mkdir). commands only has the one gate command.

Test retryWithAgent:false:
- blocking: gate throws once → return {success:false, failedGate, error}; commands length 1 (no mkdir, no run-agent).
- non-blocking: two gates [retry-no (blocking:false), next (ok)] → success true, nonBlockingFailures [name], next gate ran.

Test non-recoverable: gate fails with error text containing 'Bad credentials':
- blocking → {success:false, failedGate, error contains 'Bad credentials'}; commands: gate cmd + mkdir? wait — resumeAgent: isNonRecoverable checked BEFORE ensureFeedbackDir → no mkdir. So commands = [gate cmd].
- non-blocking → nonBlockingFailures entry; warn path '(no resume attempted)'.

Test attempts-exhausted: pre-set files['outputs/feedback/TS-xh_quality_gate_x.atempt'] = '2', maxAttempts 2 → gate throws → resume attempted=false (exhausted) → blocking failure; commands [gate cmd] only.

Test returnAfterResume (3 sources): each → {success:false, resumeAttempted:true, ...}; commands include mkdir + run-agent.sh; marker '1'.
- options: { returnAfterResume: true }
- gate: { returnAfterResume: true }
- config: feedbackLoop: { qualityGates: { returnAfterResume: true, ... }

Test non-Error throws: cli throws 'plain fail' → blocking failure error === 'plain fail'. Also throw object {custom:'x'} without message → String({custom:'x'}) === '[object Object]'.

Test output null → ': command returns null → results[0].output === ''. The default mock returns '' — || '' → ''. Use custom mock returning null.

Test results shape: [{name:'a', success:true, attempts:1, output:''}, ...]. And after non-blocking failure: {name:'spot', success:false, attempts:2, error:..., blocking:false} — attempts: gate maxAttempts 1 → fail(1) → resume → fail(2) → attempts>1 → non-blocking record with attempts 2.

Test legacy root-section array: customParams: { qualityGates: [{name:'legacy', command:'echo legacy'}] } via runQualityGates → ran. Hmm wait — getConfiguredGates(customParams, section='qualityGates', legacyKey='qualityGates'): config = normalizeConfig(customParams, 'qualityGates') — root keys copied: customParams.qualityGates is array → copied to merged.qualityGates; scoped = root.qualityGates (array, typeof object) → Object.keys of array → merged['0'], merged['1']... then gates = config.gates (undefined) || config['qualityGates'] (the array!) → ✓ runs.

Test section-named array: customParams: { feedbackLoop: { qualityGates: [{name:'sec', command:'echo sec'}] } → same path — also merged.qualityGates. Hmm — both tests hit the same `config[section]` branch. The `customParams[legacyKey]` distinct branch: gates must come from customParams[legacyKey] where legacyKey = section — when normalizeConfig does NOT produce config[section]... e.g. customParams: { qualityGates: [...] } DOES produce config[section] (root copy). To hit the third fallback: need config.gates and config[section] both falsy but customParams[section] truthy — impossible since normalizeConfig copies root arrays... UNLESS customParams[section] is a non-array non-null value like a STRING? normalizeConfig: `typeof root[key] !== 'object'` → string copied → config[section] = string → truthy → gates = string → not array → []. Hmm.

What about legacyKey different from section? getConfiguredGates(customParams, section, legacyKey) — called as (customParams, options.section || section, section) — legacyKey ALWAYS === section in runConfiguredGates. And runFeedbackLoop's other call? getConfiguredGates is only called from runConfiguredGates. So the third term fires only when config.gates and config[section] are both falsy while customParams[section] is truthy — given normalizeConfig copies arrays/scalars from root, config[section] truthy whenever customParams[section] truthy... EXCEPT when customParams[section] is null/undefined/false/'' (falsy) — then third term also falsy. So the third term is DEAD in practice — unreachable? Actually if customParams[legacyKey] is an ARRAY: config[section] = that array (truthy) → second term wins. If it's an object: normalizeConfig skips objects (typeof object && !array → not copied) → config[section] falsy; scoped = root[section] (object) → merged gets its keys (maybe gates!) → config.gates could win. If scoped object has no gates and root has no gates... then customParams[legacyKey] = object truthy → gates = the OBJECT → not array → []. Covers the third TERM being truthy but non-array → []. 

So to cover the third term of `||`: customParams: { qualityGates: { gates: undefined }... normalizeConfig({qualityGates: {...}}, 'qualityGates'): root keys — qualityGates is plain object → skipped; scoped = the object → keys copied (gates: undefined → merged.gates = undefined). gates = config.gates (undefined) || config['qualityGates'] (undefined) || customParams['qualityGates'] (the OBJECT — truthy) → object → not array → []. ✓ Covers third term. Test: gates object → success true, zero commands.

And Array.isArray false branch — covered by same test.

OK. Now — `options.section` override path: add a test passing options: { section: 'qualityGates' } explicitly → behaves the same. Covers left arm of `options.section || section` (all existing tests cover right arm).

Now the review_verdict characterization tests (as listed). Let me also double check `unwrap(io.exec(...))` — ioStub wraps execSt.exec with unwrap already (`exec: function (cmd) { return unwrap(execSt.exec(cmd)); }`). And module unwrap then... In applyReviewVerdict, `unwrap(io.exec(...))` — io.exec returns STRING (already unwrapped by ioStub)…

Both entry points only use the public API — safe to refactor internals. Now **TDD phase 1 (characterization)**: pin every currently-uncovered branch of both functions with tests that must pass against the CURRENT code. Adding the `runConfiguredGates` suite first:

Note CRAP formula in crap4js: crap = comp^2 * (1-cov)^3 + comp. Check: 37^2*(0.151)^3 + 37 = 1369*0.00344 + 37 = 4.71+37 = 41.7 ✓. For applyReviewVerdict: 39^2*(0.015)^3+39 = 1521*3.4e-6+39 ≈ 39.0 ✓.

So for runConfiguredGates: to get CRAP <= 8, with full coverage and complexity C: CRAP = C. So I need complexity <= 8 AND 100% coverage. Alternatively CRAP<=8 tolerates e.g. comp 7 with coverage 99.3%: 49*(0.007)^3 ≈ 1.7e-5, CRAP≈7. Practically: reduce complexity and cover everything.

Plan for `runConfiguredGates` (comp 37): extract pure helpers:
- `resolveGateCommand(gate, ticketKey)` → command string or null
- `resolveGateWorkingDir(gate, options, config)` 
- `gateMaxAttempts(gate)` 
- `buildGateFeedbackConfig(section, gate, maxAttempts)` → feedbackLoopConfig object
- `buildGateResumeOptions(options, section, stagePrefix, name, gate, maxAttempts, command, workingDir, errorText)` → resumeAgent options... 
- `gateFailureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures)` → the blocking failure return object
- `nonBlockingFailure(gateType, name, attempts, errorText)` handling — pushes to results/nonBlockingFailures (impure-ish but fine as helper taking arrays)
- The per-gate run loop → maybe extract `runSingleGate(gate, ctx)` returning either {done:true,...} or continuation info.

The loop structure: for each gate → skip disabled/skippable → while(true) attempts++ → run → on error: if attempts>max || noRetry → non-blocking? record : return failure; else resume → if !resume.atempted → non-blocking? record : return failure; if returnAfterResume → return failure+resumeAttempted; else loop again.

A clean decomposition:

```js
function failureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   return { success: false, failedGate: name, error: errorText, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}

function recordNonBlockingFailure(name, attempts, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   console.warn(...);
   results.push({ name: name, success: false, attempts: attempts, error: errorText, blocking: false });
   nonBlockingFailures.push({ name: name, error: errorText });
}
``

`runGateAttempt(gate, name, command, workingDir, gateType)` → try runCommand, log; return {ok:true, output} or {ok:false, errorText}.

`shouldRetryGate(gate, attempts, maxAttempts)` → attempts <= max && gate.retryWithAgent !== false.

`gateResumeCustomParams(section, gate, maxAttempts)`.

Then runConfiguredGates:

```js
function runConfiguredGates(options, section, stagePrefix) {
   options = options || {};
   section = section || 'qualityGates';
   stagePrefix = stagePrefix || 'quality_gate';
   var gateType = section === 'policyGates' ? 'policy gate' : 'quality gate';
   var customParams = options.customParams || {};
   var config = normalizeConfig(customParams, options.section || section);
   var gates = getConfiguredGates(customParams, options.section || section, section);
   var results = [];
   var nonBlockingFailures = [];
   for (var i = 0; i < gates.length; i++) {
       var outcome = runGate(gates[i], i, { options, section, stagePrefix, gateType, config, customParams, results, nonBlockingFailures });
       if (outcome) return outcome; // a failure result to bubble
   }
   return { success: true, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}
``

And runGate contains the while loop; its complexity: conditions: gate && gate.enabled===false (2), command truthy, while loop, try/catch, attempts>max||retryWithAgent===false (2), !isBlocking, resume.atempted, returnAfterResume||...||... (2). Roughly ~11-12. With full coverage CRAP ~11-12 > 8. Need to split more.

Split the catch-handling into a helper: `handleGateFailure(...)` that returns either null (retry) or a result object. Then runGate's complexity shrinks.

Let me carefully plan to keep behavior identical: "Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order."

Behavior details to preserve:
1. console.log('Running ' + gateType + ' "' + name + '": ' + command) BEFORE each runCommand attempt (including retries).
2. On success: results.push({name, success:true, attempts, output: output || ''}). Note `runCommand(...) || ''` — output coerced to ''.
3. On throw: errorText = e && e.message ? e.message : String(e).
4. If attempts > maxAttempts || gate.retryWithAgent === false:
  - non-blocking: warn + push result + nonBlockingFailures, break (continue next gate)
  - blocking: return failure object.
5. Else resume via resumeAgent with config {feedbackLoop: {[section]: {enabled:true, maxAttempts, resumeArgs: gate.resumeArgs || undefined, nonRecoverablePatterns: gate.nonRecoverablePatterns || undefined}}, stage = stagePrefix + '_' + name, error = 'Command failed: ' + command + (workingDir ? '\nWorking directory: ' + workingDir : '') + '\n' + errorText.
  - if !resume.atempted: non-blocking? warn+record+break : return failure
  - if options.returnAfterResume || config.returnAfterResume || gate.returnAfterResume: return failure + resumeAttempted:true

Note CRAP formula in crap4js: crap = comp^2 * (1-cov)^3 + comp. Check: 37^2*(0.151)^3 + 37 = 1369*0.00344 + 37 = 4.71+37 = 41.7 ✓. For applyReviewVerdict: 39^2*(0.015)^3+39 = 1521*3.4e-6+39 ≈ 39.0 ✓.

So for runConfiguredGates: to get CRAP <= 8, with full coverage and complexity C: CRAP = C. So I need complexity <= 8 AND 100% coverage. Alternatively CRAP<=8 tolerates e.g. comp 7 with coverage 99.3%: 49*(0.007)^3 ≈ 1.7e-5, CRAP≈7. Practically: reduce complexity and cover everything.

Plan for `runConfiguredGates` (comp 37): extract pure helpers:
- `resolveGateCommand(gate, ticketKey)` → command string or null
- `resolveGateWorkingDir(gate, options, config)` 
- `gateMaxAttempts(gate)` 
- `buildGateFeedbackConfig(section, gate, maxAttempts)` → feedbackLoopConfig object
- `buildGateResumeOptions(options, section, stagePrefix, name, gate, maxAttempts, command, workingDir, errorText)` → resumeAgent options... 
- `gateFailureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures)` → the blocking failure return object
- `nonBlockingFailure(gateType, name, attempts, errorText)` handling — pushes to results/nonBlockingFailures (impure-ish but fine as helper taking arrays)
- The per-gate run loop → maybe extract `runSingleGate(gate, ctx)` returning either {done:true,...} or continuation info.

The loop structure: for each gate → skip disabled/skippable → while(true) attempts++ → run → on error: if attempts>max || noRetry → non-blocking? record : return failure; else resume → if !resume.atempted → non-blocking? record : return failure; if returnAfterResume → return failure+resumeAttempted; else loop again.

A clean decomposition:

```js
function failureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {

}

function recordNonBlockingFailure(name, attempts, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {

}

- The per-gate run loop → maybe extract `runSingleGate(gate, ctx)` returning either {done:true,...} or continuation info.

The loop structure: for each gate → skip disabled/skippable → while(true) attempts++ → run → on error: if attempts>max || noRetry → non-blocking? record : return failure; else resume → if !resume.atempted → non-blocking? record : return failure; if returnAfterResume → return failure+resumeAttempted; else loop again.

A clean decomposition:

```js
function failureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   return { success: false, failedGate: name, error: errorText, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}

function recordNonBlockingFailure(name, attempts, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   console.warn(...);
   results.push({ name: name, success: false, attempts: attempts, error: errorText, blocking: false });
   nonBlockingFailures.push({ name: name, error: errorText });
}
``

`runGateAttempt(gate, name, command, workingDir, gateType)` → try runCommand, log; return {ok:true, output} or {ok:false, errorText}.

`shouldRetryGate(gate, attempts, maxAttempts)` → attempts <= max && gate.retryWithAgent !== false.

```js
function runConfiguredGates(options, section, stagePrefix) {
   options = options || {};
   section = section || 'qualityGates';
   stagePrefix = stagePrefix || 'quality_gate';
   var gateType = section === 'policyGates' ? 'policy gate' : 'quality gate';
   var customParams = options.customParams || {};
   var config = normalizeConfig(customParams, options.section || section);
   var gates = getConfiguredGates(customParams, options.section || section, section);
   var results = [];
   var nonBlockingFailures = [];
   for (var i = 0; i < gates.length; i++) {
       var outcome = runGate(gates[i], i, { options, section, stagePrefix, gateType, config, customParams, results, nonBlockingFailures });
       if (outcome) return outcome; // a failure result to bubble
   }
   return { success: true, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}
``

1. console.log('Running ' + gateType + ' "' + name + '": ' + command) BEFORE each runCommand attempt (including retries).
2. On success: results.push({name, success:true, attempts, output: output || ''}). Note `runCommand(...) || ''` — output coerced to ''.
3. On throw: errorText = e && e.message ? e.message : String(e).

'\nWorking directory: ' + workingDir : '') + '\n' + errorText.
  - if !resume.atempted: non-blocking? warn+record+break : return failure

Plan for `runConfiguredGates` (comp 37): extract pure helpers:
- `resolveGateCommand(gate, ticketKey)` → command string or null
- `resolveGateWorkingDir(gate, options, config)` 
- `gateMaxAttempts(gate)` 
- `buildGateFeedbackConfig(section, gate, maxAttempts)` → feedbackLoopConfig object
- `buildGateResumeOptions(options, section, stagePrefix, name, gate, maxAttempts, command, workingDir, errorText)` → resumeAgent options... 
- `gateFailureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures)` → the blocking failure return object
- `nonBlockingFailure(gateType, name, attempts, errorText)` handling — pushes to results/nonBlockingFailures (impure-ish but fine as helper taking arrays)
- The per-gate run loop → maybe extract `runSingleGate(gate, ctx)` returning either {done:true,...} or continuation info.

The loop structure: for each gate → skip disabled/skippable → while(true) attempts++ → run → on error: if attempts>max || noRetry → non-blocking? record : return failure; else resume → if !resume.atempted → non-blocking? record : return failure; if returnAfterResume → return failure+resumeAttempted; else loop again.

A clean decomposition:

```js
function failureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   return { success: false, failedGate: name, error: errorText, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}

function recordNonBlockingFailure(name, attempts, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   console.warn(...);
   results.push({ name: name, success: false, attempts: attempts, error: errorText, blocking: false });
   nonBlockingFailures.push({ name: name, error: errorText });
}
``

`runGateAttempt(gate, name, command, workingDir, gateType)` → try runCommand, log; return {ok:true, output} or {ok:false, errorText}.

`shouldRetryGate(gate, attempts, maxAttempts)` → attempts <= max && gate.retryWithAgent !== false.

`gateResumeCustomParams(section, gate, maxAttempts)`.

Then runConfiguredGates:

```js
function runConfiguredGates(options, section, stagePrefix) {
   options = options || {};
   section = section || 'qualityGates';
   stagePrefix = stagePrefix || 'quality_gate';
   var gateType = section === 'policyGates' ? 'policy gate' : 'quality gate';
   var customParams = options.customParams || {};
   var config = normalizeConfig(customParams, options.section || section);
   var gates = getConfiguredGates(customParams, options.section || section, section);
   var results = [];
   var nonBlockingFailures = [];
   for (var i = 0; i < gates.length; i++) {
       var outcome = runGate(gates[i], i, { options, section, stagePrefix, gateType, config, customParams, results, nonBlockingFailures });
       if (outcome) return outcome; // a failure result to bubble
   }
   return { success: true, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}
``

And runGate contains the while loop; its complexity: conditions: gate && gate.enabled===false (2), command truthy, while loop, try/catch, attempts>max||retryWithAgent===false (2), !isBlocking, resume.atempted, returnAfterResume||...||... Split the catch-handling into a helper: `handleGateFailure(...)` that returns either null (retry) or a result object. Then runGate's complexity shrinks.

Behavior details to preserve:
1. console.log('Running ' + gateType + ' "' + name + '": ' + command) BEFORE each runCommand attempt (including retries).
2. On success: results.push({name, success:true, attempts, output: output || ''}). Note `runCommand(...) || ''` — output coerced to ''.
3. On throw: errorText = e && e.message ? e.message : String(e).
4. If attempts > maxAttempts || gate.retryWithAgent === false:
  - non-blocking: warn + push result + nonBlockingFailures, break (continue next gate)
  - blocking: return failure object.
5. Else resume via resumeAgent with config {feedbackLoop: {[section]: {enabled:true, maxAttempts, resumeArgs: gate.resumeArgs || undefined, nonRecoverablePatterns: gate.nonRecoverablePatterns || undefined}}, stage = stagePrefix + '_' + name, error = 'Command failed: ' + command + (workingDir ? '\nWorking directory: ' + workingDir : '') + '\n' + errorText.
  - if !resume.atempted: non-blocking? warn+record+break : return failure

Plan for `runConfiguredGates` (comp 37): extract pure helpers:
- `resolveGateCommand(gate, ticketKey)` → command string or null
- `resolveGateWorkingDir(gate, options, config)`

- `gateFailureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures)` → the blocking failure return object
- `nonBlockingFailure(gateType, name, attempts, errorText)` handling — pushes to results/nonBlockingFailures (impure-ish but fine as helper taking arrays)
- The per-gate run loop → maybe extract `runSingleGate(gate, ctx)` returning either {done:true,...} or continuation info.

The loop structure: for each gate → skip disabled/skippable → while(true) attempts++ → run → on error: if attempts>max || noRetry → non-blocking? record : return failure; else resume → if !resume.atempted → non-blocking? record : return failure; if returnAfterResume → return failure+resumeAttempted; else loop again.

function failureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {

}

function recordNonBlockingFailure(name, attempts, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {

}

Also visible: overall stats. Let me capture the "before" report of CRAP max and count above 8 across the repo.

Note CRAP formula in crap4js: crap = comp^2 * (1-cov)^3 + comp. Check: 37^2*(0.151)^3 + 37 = 1369*0.00344 + 37 = 4.71+37 = 41.7 ✓. For applyReviewVerdict: 39^2*(0.015)^3+39 = 1521*3.4e-6+39 ≈ 39.0 ✓.

So for runConfiguredGates: to get CRAP <= 8, with full coverage and complexity C: CRAP = C. So I need complexity <= 8 AND 100% coverage. Alternatively CRAP<=8 tolerates e.g. comp 7 with coverage 99.3%: 49*(0.007)^3 ≈ 1.7e-5, CRAP≈7. Practically: reduce complexity and cover everything.

Plan for `runConfiguredGates` (comp 37): extract pure helpers:
- `resolveGateCommand(gate, ticketKey)` → command string or null
- `resolveGateWorkingDir(gate, options, config)` 
- `gateMaxAttempts(gate)` 
- `buildGateFeedbackConfig(section, gate, maxAttempts)` → feedbackLoopConfig object
- `buildGateResumeOptions(options, section, stagePrefix, name, gate, maxAttempts, command, workingDir, errorText)` → resumeAgent options... 
- `gateFailureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures)` → the blocking failure return object
- `nonBlockingFailure(gateType, name, attempts, errorText)` handling — pushes to results/nonBlockingFailures (impure-ish but fine as helper taking arrays)
- The per-gate run loop → maybe extract `runSingleGate(gate, ctx)` returning either {done:true,...} or continuation info.

The loop structure: for each gate → skip disabled/skippable → while(true) attempts++ → run → on error: if attempts>max || noRetry → non-blocking? record : return failure; else resume → if !resume.atempted → non-blocking? record : return failure; if returnAfterResume → return failure+resumeAttempted; else loop again.

A clean decomposition:

```js
function failureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   return { success: false, failedGate: name, error: errorText, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}

function recordNonBlockingFailure(name, attempts, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   console.warn(...);
   results.push({ name: name, success: false, attempts: attempts, error: errorText, blocking: false });
   nonBlockingFailures.push({ name: name, error: errorText });
}
``

`runGateAttempt(gate, name, command, workingDir, gateType)` → try runCommand, log; return {ok:true, output} or {ok:false, errorText}.

`shouldRetryGate(gate, attempts, maxAttempts)` → attempts <= max && gate.retryWithAgent !== false.

`gateResumeCustomParams(section, gate, maxAttempts)`.

Then runConfiguredGates:

```js
function runConfiguredGates(options, section, stagePrefix) {
   options = options || {};
   section = section || 'qualityGates';
   stagePrefix = stagePrefix || 'quality_gate';
   var gateType = section === 'policyGates' ? 'policy gate' : 'quality gate';
   var customParams = options.customParams || {};
   var config = normalizeConfig(customParams, options.section || section);
   var gates = getConfiguredGates(customParams, options.section || section, section);
   var results = [];
   var nonBlockingFailures = [];
   for (var i = 0; i < gates.length; i++) {
       var outcome = runGate(gates[i], i, { options, section, stagePrefix, gateType, config, customParams, results, nonBlockingFailures });
       if (outcome) return outcome; // a failure result to bubble
   }
   return { success: true, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}
``

And runGate contains the while loop; its complexity: conditions: gate && gate.enabled===false (2), command truthy, while loop, try/catch, attempts>max||retryWithAgent===false (2), !isBlocking, resume.atempted, returnAfterResume||...||... (2). Roughly ~11-12. With full coverage CRAP ~11-12 > 8. Need to split more.

Split the catch-handling into a helper: `handleGateFailure(...)` that returns either null (retry) or a result object. Then runGate's complexity shrinks.

Let me carefully plan to keep behavior identical: "Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order."

Behavior details to preserve:
1. console.log('Running ' + gateType + ' "' + name + '": ' + command) BEFORE each runCommand attempt (including retries).
2. On success: results.push({name, success:true, attempts, output: output || ''}). Note `runCommand(...) || ''` — output coerced to ''.
3. On throw: errorText = e && e.message ? e.message : String(e).
4. If attempts > maxAttempts || gate.retryWithAgent === false:
  - non-blocking: warn + push result + nonBlockingFailures, break (continue next gate)
  - blocking: return failure object.
5. Else resume via resumeAgent with config {feedbackLoop: {[section]: {enabled:true, maxAttempts, resumeArgs: gate.resumeArgs || undefined, nonRecoverablePatterns: gate.nonRecoverablePatterns || undefined}}, stage = stagePrefix + '_' + name, error = 'Command failed: ' + command + (workingDir ? '\nWorking directory: ' + workingDir : '') + '\n' + errorText.
  - if !resume.atempted: non-blocking? warn+record+break : return failure
  - if options.returnAfterResume || config.returnAfterResume || gate.returnAfterResume: return failure + resumeAttempted:true
6. Note subtlety: maxAttempts parsed as `parseInt(gate.maxAttempts, 10) || 0` — 0 means while(true) never resumes (atempts>max always true on first failure → immediate failure path). Note `maxAttempts = parseInt(...) || 0` vs resumeAgent's handling. Keep exact.

Note: in the current code, `results.push` for non-blocking success: false includes `atempts: attempts` where attempts is incremented count. And error message in warn: '⚠️ Non-blocking ' + gateType + ' "' + name + '" failed after ' + attempts + ' attempt(s) — continuing without blocking: ' + errorText. And the no-resume variant: '⚠️ Non-blocking ' + gateType + ' "' + name + '" failed (no resume attempted) — continuing without blocking: ' + errorText.

Also there's a subtle case: attempts <= maxAttempts but retryWithAgent === false → non-blocking warn says "failed after N attempt(s)" variant.

Note CRAP formula in crap4js: crap = comp^2 * (1-cov)^3 + comp. Check: 37^2*(0.151)^3 + 37 = 1369*0.00344 + 37 = 4.71+37 = 41.7 ✓. For applyReviewVerdict: 39^2*(0.015)^3+39 = 1521*3.4e-6+39 ≈ 39.0 ✓.

So for runConfiguredGates: to get CRAP <= 8, with full coverage and complexity C: CRAP = C. So I need complexity <= 8 AND 100% coverage. Alternatively CRAP<=8 tolerates e.g. comp 7 with coverage 99.3%: 49*(0.007)^3 ≈ 1.7e-5, CRAP≈7. Practically: reduce complexity and cover everything.

Plan for `runConfiguredGates` (comp 37): extract pure helpers:
- `resolveGateCommand(gate, ticketKey)` → command string or null
- `resolveGateWorkingDir(gate, options, config)` 
- `gateMaxAttempts(gate)` 
- `buildGateFeedbackConfig(section, gate, maxAttempts)` → feedbackLoopConfig object
- `buildGateResumeOptions(options, section, stagePrefix, name, gate, maxAttempts, command, workingDir, errorText)` → resumeAgent options... 
- `gateFailureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures)` → the blocking failure return object
- `nonBlockingFailure(gateType, name, attempts, errorText)` handling — pushes to results/nonBlockingFailures (impure-ish but fine as helper taking arrays)
- The per-gate run loop → maybe extract `runSingleGate(gate, ctx)` returning either {done:true,...} or continuation info.

The loop structure: for each gate → skip disabled/skippable → while(true) attempts++ → run → on error: if attempts>max || noRetry → non-blocking? record : return failure; else resume → if !resume.atempted → non-blocking? record : return failure; if returnAfterResume → return failure+resumeAttempted; else loop again.

A clean decomposition:

```js
function failureResult(name, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   return { success: false, failedGate: name, error: errorText, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}

function recordNonBlockingFailure(name, attempts, errorText, results, nonBlockingFailures) {
   console.warn(...);
   results.push({ name: name, success: false, attempts: attempts, error: errorText, blocking: false });
   nonBlockingFailures.push({ name: name, error: errorText });
}
``

`runGateAttempt(gate, name, command, workingDir, gateType)` → try runCommand, log; return {ok:true, output} or {ok:false, errorText}.

`shouldRetryGate(gate, attempts, maxAttempts)` → attempts <= max && gate.retryWithAgent !== false.

`gateResumeCustomParams(section, gate, maxAttempts)`.

Then runConfiguredGates:

```js
function runConfiguredGates(options, section, stagePrefix) {
   options = options || {};
   section = section || 'qualityGates';
   stagePrefix = stagePrefix || 'quality_gate';
   var gateType = section === 'policyGates' ? 'policy gate' : 'quality gate';
   var customParams = options.customParams || {};
   var config = normalizeConfig(customParams, options.section || section);
   var gates = getConfiguredGates(customParams, options.section || section, section);
   var results = [];
   var nonBlockingFailures = [];
   for (var i = 0; i < gates.length; i++) {
       var outcome = runGate(gates[i], i, { options, section, stagePrefix, gateType, config, customParams, results, nonBlockingFailures });
       if (outcome) return outcome; // a failure result to bubble
   }
   return { success: true, results: results, nonBlockingFailures: nonBlockingFailures };
}
``

And runGate contains the while loop; its complexity: conditions: gate && gate.enabled===false (2), command truthy, while loop, try/catch, attempts>max||retryWithAgent===false (2), !isBlocking, resume.atempted, returnAfterResume||...||... (2). Roughly ~11-12. With full coverage CRAP ~11-12 > 8. Need to split more.

Split the catch-handling into a helper: `handleGateFailure(...)` that returns either null (retry) or a result object. Then runGate's complexity shrinks.

Let me carefully plan to keep behavior identical: "Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order."

Behavior details to preserve:
1. console.log('Running ' + gateType + ' "' + name + '": ' + command) BEFORE each runCommand attempt (including retries).
2. On success: results.push({name, success:true, attempts, output: output || ''}). Note `runCommand(...) || ''` — output coerced to ''.
3. On throw: errorText = e && e.message ? e.message : String(e).
4. If attempts > maxAttempts || gate.retryWithAgent === false:
  - non-blocking: warn + push result + nonBlockingFailures, break (continue next gate)
  - blocking: return failure object.
